V5-14.10.text: An approved replacement MUST retain its immutable successor bytes in the same source revision chain (append exactly once, or reuse the pinned already-accepted proposal revision), advance its approved mutation head, publish its immediate or scheduled valid-time transition/review, increment the control version, and invalidate affected claims/views/index/cache entries in one coordinator application. The logical coordinator effect is `source_revision_transition`; its persisted encoding must be registered in the existing effect system.

V5-14.11.section_title: Corrections, supersession, and the stale-deploy demonstration
V5-14.11.text: Mutation MUST compare both the selected predecessor source revision and source-state control version with the live approved mutation head/state under the transaction. A historical or currently displayed predecessor of an already approved future transition is not that mutation head; it needs explicit inspection/resolution rather than blind overwrite. Pending proposals may reference newly accepted revisions but MUST NOT advance the approved head; their receipts distinguish `change_state` in `{not_requested, proposed, applied, blocked}` from source acceptance/readiness. A restricted agent cannot select the reviewer or turn a proposal into applied state.

V5-14.12.blocker: v5 spec not yet approved — implementation unauthorized (V5-00.01)
V5-14.12.note: supersede/effective_at: commit-time default, future effective time schedules eligibility (read-time evaluation, no wake-job dependency).
V5-14.12.section_title: Corrections, supersession, and the stale-deploy demonstration
V5-14.12.text: `supersede` declares a change from the predecessor to successor at `effective_at`; when omitted, use the authenticated explicit operation's commit time as the declared effective time, not a parsed timestamp invented from prose.
